The DC Dark Multiverse is a concept in the DC Comics universe introduced around 2018 during an event called "Dark Nights: Metal." It exists as a parallel universe to the regular DC Multiverse, consisting of infinite worlds that embody the fears, failures, and dark desires of characters from the main multiverse. These worlds are unstable, constantly collapsing on themselves due to their inherently flawed nature.

The Dark Multiverse is ruled by an evil deity known as Perpetua, who was once imprisoned in the Source Wall—an outer boundary separating the multiverse from chaos—but she escaped in the "Doomsday Clock" series. The most notable figure from the Dark Multiverse is the Batman Who Laughs, a sinister version of Batman who was infected with Joker venom and became a hybrid of the two. He emerged as one of the most prominent antagonists, attempting to conquer the main multiverse with help from similarly dark versions of famous heroes.

While certain figures can travel freely between the Dark Multiverse and the regular Multiverse, those attempts often result in catastrophic events, as witnessed when the Dark Multiverse became part of the plotline involving Anti-Monitor and Earth-3's Crime Syndicate of America.

The DC Dark Multiverse is a concept within DC Comics introduced during the "Dark Nights: Metal" storyline. It is essentially a series of alternate realities that exist beneath the regular DC Multiverse, characterized by twisted versions of iconic DC stories and characters. The Dark Multiverse is overseen by the cosmic entity known as the Monitor and is populated by various Dark Knights, who are evil versions of Batman that have been twisted by their greatest fears turning into reality.

The most prominent character from the Dark Multiverse is the Batman Who Laughs, a fusion of Batman and the Joker, who hails from one of these dark worlds. In these realms, universes are unstable and prone to collapse, and they represent the greatest fears and failures of the heroes in the main DC Universe. Events in the Dark Multiverse can influence the main universe, although they don't follow traditional comic book logic, often resulting in bizarre or tragic outcomes.

Unlike the main multiverse, which consists of only 52 universes, the Dark Multiverse contains an infinite number of realities. The stories from the Dark Multiverse are usually narrated by Krona, a rogue Guardian of the Universe. These stories are separate from the main continuity and allow DC Comics to explore "what if" scenarios in which famous events took very different, often darker paths.

The DC Dark Multiverse is a concept in the DC Comics universe that refers to a vast, uncharted expanse of alternate realities that exist outside of the mainstream DC Multiverse. It was introduced in the 2017-2018 comic book series "Dark Nights: Metal" by Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo.

The Dark Multiverse is a realm of twisted, nightmarish worlds that are born from the darkest fears and nightmares of the DC Universe. These worlds are the result of choices and events that went horribly wrong, creating realities that are often the opposite of the mainstream DC Universe.

Each world in the Dark Multiverse is a twisted reflection of a familiar DC reality, with characters and events that are distorted and corrupted. For example, the Dark Multiverse contains worlds where the Justice League is evil, where Batman is a villain, or where the DC Universe is ruled by dark, malevolent forces.

The Dark Multiverse is also home to the Dark Knights, a group of twisted, evil versions of Batman from different realities. These Dark Knights are the main antagonists of the "Dark Nights: Metal" series and are led by the Batman Who Laughs, a twisted version of Batman who has been infected by the Joker's toxin.

The DC Dark Multiverse has been explored in various comic book series and storylines, including "Dark Nights: Metal," "The Batman Who Laughs," and "Tales from the Dark Multiverse." It has also been referenced in other DC media, such as the animated series "Justice League Dark: Apokolips War."

Overall, the DC Dark Multiverse is a rich and complex concept that adds depth and complexity to the DC Universe, exploring the darker corners of the DC Multiverse and the infinite possibilities of the DC cosmos.

The DC Dark Multiverse is a concept introduced in DC Comics as part of the larger multiverse structure. Unlike the regular multiverse, which contains alternate realities that exist in parallel to the primary DC Universe, the Dark Multiverse is a realm of unstable and impermanent worlds originating from the fears and failures of beings within the main multiverse. It was first explored in the comic series "Dark Days: The Forge" and "Dark Nights: Metal", published in the 1980s, which introduced the character Barbatos, an ancient bat god responsible for maintaining the Dark Multiverse.

These worlds are typically dystopian or catastrophic versions of existing DC universes and are continually in flux because they stem from negative emotions and dark possibilities. A notable aspect of the Dark Multiverse is its influence on the main multiverse, illustrated by the rise of dark versions of Batman, such as The Batman Who Laughs, who are twisted amalgamations of Batman with his greatest foes. 

The Dark Multiverse’s visual representation is depicted as bright and vibrant, contrasting the more subdued visuals of the main multiverse, to symbolize its impermanence and chaotic nature. This realm interacts with the multiverse above through breaches that happen during significant crises or when characters actively seek it out.
